titulo: Why a torn QR code still works 🔳
descripcion: QR codes store extra recovery data using Reed–Solomon error correction. At the highest level, up to about 30% can be damaged and still scan.

escenas.texto: Rip off a corner of a QR code, and it still scans. How is that possible?
QR codes hide extra backup data inside the pattern, using a math trick called Reed Solomon error correction.

panel.label: Extra backup data inside the pattern

escenas.texto: At the highest level, up to about thirty percent of the code can be damaged, and the scanner rebuilds the missing part.
That's why some brands put a logo right in the middle. The code simply recovers the hidden squares.
The same math protects CDs, satellite signals and space probes. Follow for more hidden tech.
